questions.prompt: How should clients create email jobs?
questions.description: The current POST /api/emails waits for mock delivery and returns a sent email. A separate route can preserve that behavior.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Add POST /api/email-jobs; keep POST /api/emails synchronous. Return the queued job ID and scheduled time with 202 Accepted.

questions.prompt: Which retry policy should email jobs use after a processing error?
questions.description: pg-boss supports retryLimit, retryDelay, and exponential backoff. This applies to failures from validation, delivery, or persistence unless the implementation distinguishes them.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Retry unexpected processing failures up to 3 times, starting after 60 seconds with exponential backoff; reject invalid payloads without retry.

options.label: 3 retries, 60-second exponential backoff; invalid payloads fail immediately
3 retries, fixed 60-second delay; invalid payloads fail immediately

questions.prompt: What should the database activity log record?
questions.description: The queue stores its own job state. This question defines the application-owned history and whether clients can read it.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Append a row for job creation, each processing start, each failed attempt, and completion or final failure; expose a GET /api/email-jobs/:id endpoint with status and ordered activity.

options.label: All lifecycle events, plus status and activity API
All lifecycle events in DB; no read API yet
One outcome per attempt in DB; no read API yet

questions.prompt: What delivery guarantee is acceptable when a worker crashes after sending but before recording completion?
questions.description: pg-boss can retry a job after a crash. The existing email client and sent-email repository do not support provider-level idempotency.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Accept at-least-once delivery for this first mock-backed implementation; document that a retry can send twice after a crash.

options.label: Accept possible duplicate sends for now
